fields.explanation: The official Salesforce product page directly describes Salesforce as a customer relationship management platform bringing together people, AI agents, apps, and data.
Official Salesforce documentation explicitly identifies per-user OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, supporting oauth2 as an available authentication method.

Official documentation says Developer Edition is free for testing and development and instructs users to sign up, create an external client app in a Salesforce org, enable OAuth, and configure an OAuth flow.
The official quick-start documentation explicitly establishes a Connect REST API.
The unknown value is appropriate because the record explicitly states that no supplied API index or adequate reference established the number of resource families or workflows.
Official Salesforce documentation describes Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers and states that they use the open Model Context Protocol standard.

Official documentation establishes a usable Connect REST API, a free Developer Edition path, external-client-app OAuth setup, access-token acquisition, and authenticated API requests. No blocker is stated, so the ready verdict is supported.

Zendesk’s official site directly describes it as an AI-first service platform, identifies both customer and employee service offerings, and states that customer enquiries are resolved across all channels.

Official authentication documentation states that API tokens are supported and that Basic authentication is used when sending API-token credentials. It also notes that API tokens are deprecated, but they remain documented as usable for existing customers.

Official documentation requires a verified user, lists a Zendesk Support account with agent or admin access for the quick start, points to a free trial or sponsored testing account, and says tokens can be added through Admin Center.
Zendesk’s official Sunshine Conversations API specification explicitly says that the API is designed according to REST principles.

The official Support API reference indexes a broad set of resources, including tickets, users, organizations, workflows, business rules, account configuration, OAuth, apps, targets, side conversations, approvals, and tasks.
The cited community repository identifies itself as a Zendesk MCP server and documents tools or resources for tickets, comments, and Help Center articles.

Official sources establish a test-account path, a documented credential-management path through Admin Center, and an extensive Support/Ticketing API reference. These support the ready verdict, with no blocker claimed.
Official Slack API documentation directly states that apps and workflows can read, write, and update many types of Slack data.
Official documentation establishes Slack's OAuth 2.0 installation flow and the resulting access tokens, including bearer-token authentication for API requests.
The value is explicitly unknown, and the record states that official evidence was insufficient to determine credential-access requirements, including whether a paid plan is required.

Official documentation directly describes HTTP RPC-style Web API methods, HTTP POST event delivery to public callback endpoints (webhook-style delivery), and WebSocket communication through Socket Mode.
The official Web API reference states that it has over 200 methods, and the methods reference lists numerous method families, supporting the broad classification and notes.
An official Slack help page describes the Slack MCP server and says it gives AI assistants secure access to Slack content and actions.

Official documentation establishes the API, app-creation flow, OAuth credential path, and token acquisition, but it does not establish that no access blocker exists. The record expressly leaves paid-plan requirements unresolved, so the ready verdict with 'None evidenced' is not fully supported under the buildability standard.
Official documentation directly describes the Google Ads API as a programmatic interface for managing large or complex Google Ads accounts and campaigns.
Official documentation states that requests use OAuth 2.0 and also require a developer token.

Official documentation supports the stated requirements: developer-token sign-up, a Google Ads manager account to obtain the token, and a Google API Console project for OAuth 2.0 credentials. The unknown status is consistent with the explicitly unresolved approval and cost details.
Official documentation directly states that the API is a gRPC API with REST bindings.

The official reference and documentation enumerate a large range of resources and functions spanning campaigns, ads, assets, audiences, billing, conversions, reporting, and planning, supporting the broad classification.
The supplied official googleads repository identifies itself as the Google Ads MCP Server and documents tools and resources that interact with the Google Ads API.

Official evidence establishes the API and its broad surface, the OAuth and developer-token credential path, the manager-account and Google Cloud setup requirements, and access-level restrictions or approval steps. These support a conditional verdict and the stated access/setup blocker.
The official API overview says Shopify provides what developers need to build integrations across Shopify surfaces and lists APIs, libraries, templates, CLI tools, and frameworks.
Official documentation explicitly describes OAuth 2.0 token exchange and authorization-code grant flows, while the REST reference requires a Shopify access token.

The unknown status is appropriate: the supplied official pages describe OAuth token acquisition and apps created through the Dev Dashboard, but do not establish signup, pricing, or a complete self-service credential-creation process.
Official documentation identifies Shopify GraphQL APIs and an Admin REST API, although the REST Admin API is marked legacy.

The official API overview and GraphQL index document many resource and workflow families, including products, customers, orders, inventory, payments, events, storefronts, customer accounts, and app management.
Shopify's official documentation identifies Storefront and Customer accounts MCP servers and directly documents catalog, cart, customer-account, order-tracking, and return capabilities.

Official pages establish usable GraphQL and REST APIs and OAuth/access-token acquisition, while the record explicitly identifies the missing evidence about complete self-service credential access and commercial requirements. The conservative unknown verdict follows from that unresolved blocker.
Official documentation directly describes DataForSEO as a starting point for building SEO software, data-analysis pipelines, and no-code automations.
Official authentication documentation explicitly states that DataForSEO uses Basic Authentication and that it is the only way to access the API.
Official documentation instructs users to create a free account and retrieve the API login and automatically generated API password from the dashboard's API Access tab.
Official documentation explicitly states that the API uses REST technology over HTTP.

The official API index shows numerous distinct families, including SERP, Keywords Data, Domain Analytics, Backlinks, OnPage, App Data, Merchant, and Business Data APIs, directly supporting the broad classification and notes.
The official DataForSEO GitHub repository identifies the project as the new v3 MCP server and describes its MCP server and CLI as browsing API documentation and making authenticated API requests.

Official documentation establishes a usable REST API, multiple API families, Basic Authentication, and a self-service credential path through a free account. These support the ready verdict, with no blocker claimed.
Official GitHub documentation directly states that the API can automate processes, integrate with GitHub, and extend GitHub.
Official documentation establishes token authentication, Basic authentication for specified app endpoints, and JWT authentication, supporting token, basic, and other.

Official documentation directly supports creating a personal access token for personal use and a GitHub App for organizational or delegated use. The unknown status is acceptable because the record explicitly notes that payment requirements were not established.
Official GitHub pages directly document a REST API, a GraphQL API, and webhooks.

The official API documentation and reference navigation show many resource families, including repositories, organizations, users, issues, pull requests, Actions, and security-related resources, supporting the broad classification and notes.
The GitHub-owned repository identifies the project as GitHub's official MCP Server and documents both a GitHub-hosted remote server and a local server.

Official documentation establishes the REST API and documented endpoints, provides self-service GitHub App registration steps, and explains how to generate a private key. This supports the ready verdict and its stated reason, with no blocker claimed.
Official Notion documentation directly states that connections link a workspace to external tools and automate workflows through code.
Official documentation states that public connections use OAuth 2.0 and that internal connections and PATs use static API/bearer tokens.

Official PAT documentation shows that PATs are created in the Developer portal, workspace owners can always create API-enabled PATs, Free workspaces allow owners to create them, and other full members are governed by plan-specific workspace policy.
Official documentation explicitly identifies the REST API and documents webhook subscriptions that deliver real-time updates by HTTP POST.

Official documentation establishes broad coverage across pages, databases, data sources, comments, views, file uploads, search, users, custom emojis, and other resources; webhook event support is also documented.
Official Notion documentation identifies a hosted MCP server at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp and states that it uses OAuth authentication.

Official evidence establishes the REST API, a working PAT credential path from a Notion account through the Developer portal, availability to Free workspace owners, and the stated blocker that workspace policy can restrict PAT creation for non-owners on applicable plans.
Stripe’s official product page directly states that it helps users accept payments, offer financial services, and implement custom revenue models.
Official API documentation states that Stripe authenticates requests with API keys, while the Connect OAuth reference documents an OAuth authorization-code flow and token endpoint.

Official documentation says API keys are created when a user signs up and can be created and managed from the Developers Dashboard/API keys tab. The unknown status is acceptable because the record explicitly lacks evidence about pricing, trials, and eligibility.
The official API reference describes Stripe’s API as REST-organized, and official webhook documentation states that Stripe pushes real-time event data to registered HTTPS webhook endpoints.

The official API reference lists numerous distinct resource and product families across payments, billing, Connect, Treasury, Issuing, Tax, Identity, and other areas, directly supporting a broad classification.
Stripe’s official documentation identifies its public-preview MCP server, provides the mcp.stripe.com URL, and documents tools for Stripe API interaction and knowledge-base or documentation search.

Official evidence establishes a broad REST API and webhooks, account-based Dashboard access to API keys, and sandbox testing without affecting live data. Together these support the ready verdict, and no blocker is asserted.

Official overview directly describes Gemini Notebook Enterprise as an enterprise-ready version of an AI-powered research and writing tool that summarizes and extracts information from complex sources.

Official API examples use a bearer access token from gcloud, supporting token authentication, and official setup documentation identifies Cloud Identity and federated third-party identity frameworks, supporting the normalized 'other' category.

Official documentation requires a Google Cloud project with billing enabled, an enterprise license, Cloud NotebookLM IAM roles, and configured Cloud Identity or a third-party identity provider. The official FAQ confirms licenses are sold by subscription, supporting paid status.
The empty styles value is contradicted by official documentation that explicitly labels examples as REST and shows HTTP REST endpoints. The documented API style should not be empty.

The 'unknown' breadth value is acceptable because the pipeline explicitly records that the supplied Preview workflow pages do not establish the complete production API scope or permit a breadth classification.
The cited original third-party repository directly identifies itself as an MCP server for Google NotebookLM, supporting community status and the stated URL.

Official evidence establishes a usable REST API and bearer-token credential path. It also establishes the stated access conditions and blocker: billing-enabled project setup, administrator-managed identity/IAM, a Gemini Notebook Enterprise license, and the Cloud NotebookLM User role.
